episodes.title: The Angel's Message to Mary
episodes.description: From a silent temple to a humble hillside, the first episode follows the angelic messages that herald the births of John the Baptist and the promised Messiah. Witness Mary's faithful response and Zechariah’s restored voice as the story of salvation begins.
episodes.summary: In the temple of the Lord, the priest Zechariah offers incense when the angel Gabriel appears, bathed in radiant light. Gabriel says, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John." Zechariah, remembering his old age, questions, "How can this be, since I am old and my wife is past childbearing?" Gabriel replies that the child will be "great in the sight of the Lord" and will be filled with the Holy Spirit. Because of his doubt, Zechariah is rendered mute until the fulfillment of the promise. The angelic messenger returns six months later to a young woman named Mary in Nazareth, a virgin betrothed to Joseph. He announces, "You will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus; he will be great and called the Son of the Most High." Mary responds with humble obedience, "Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word." Soon after, Mary travels to the hill country to visit her relative Elizabeth, and when she greets her, the baby in Elizabeth’s womb leaps for joy. Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, exclaims, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb," and Mary lifts her voice in the Magnificat, praising God. Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and when the time comes for his naming, Zechariah, now able to speak, takes up a pen and declares, "His name shall be John... He will be a prophet of the Most High, preparing the way for the Lord." The people rejoice, and Zechariah prophesies, "The Lord has visited his people and given them salvation." Meanwhile, Joseph learns from a trusted source that Mary is with child, and his heart is troubled, setting the stage for the divine guidance that will follow.

episodes.title: The Birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
episodes.description: Joseph’s doubts are answered by a heavenly messenger, and a humble journey leads to the miraculous birth of the promised Messiah.
episodes.summary: Joseph, troubled by Mary's unexpected pregnancy, resolves to quietly end their betrothal. That night an angel appears to him in a dream, saying, "Take Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit" (Matt 1:20) and "She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins" (Matt 1:21). Joseph rises, filled with awe, and obeys the divine instruction. Caesar Augustus issues a decree that all should be registered for a census, requiring each person to travel to his ancestral town. Joseph, a carpenter of Nazareth, takes Mary, who is now with child, and they journey to Bethlehem, the city of David. Upon arrival they find no room in the inn, and Mary gives birth to her firstborn son, laying him in a humble manger among the straw. While shepherds tend their flocks nearby, an angel of the Lord appears, proclaiming, "Do not be afraid; I bring you good news of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord" (Lk 2:10‑11). A host of heavenly beings then fills the night sky, singing, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom He is pleased!" (Lk 2:13‑14). The shepherds look up, trembling with wonder at the celestial proclamation.

episodes.title: The Shepherds and the Wise Men
episodes.description: Shepherds hear the heavenly proclamation and find the newborn Messiah, while Mary and Joseph present Him at the temple and the Magi journey from the east to worship the King of kings.
episodes.summary: An angel appears to shepherds in the fields, saying, "Do not be afraid; I bring you good news of great joy, which will be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord" (Luke 2:10‑11). A host of heavenly beings then fills the night sky, singing, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom He is pleased!" (Luke 2:13‑14). The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem, found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger, and worshipped Him, sharing what they had heard and seen. Mary and Joseph bring the infant Jesus to the temple in Jerusalem to fulfill the Law. The devout elder Simeon, guided by the Spirit, takes the child in his arms and blesses God, saying, "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word; for mine eyes have seen thy salvation" (Luke 2:29‑30). He continues, "A sword will pierce through your own soul also," foretelling the future suffering of His mother. The family also encounters the prophetess Anna, who gives thanks to God and speaks of the child to all who were looking for redemption. Wise men from the east observe a new star and journey to Jerusalem, saying, "We have seen his star in the east and have come to worship him" (Matthew 2:2). King Herod, troubled, summons them and asks, "Where is the child who is born king of the Jews?"; he then sends them to Bethlehem. Finding the child with Mary, they present gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Matthew 2:11). That night an angel warns them in a dream, "Do not return to Herod," and they depart by another route. Soon after, an angel appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, for Herod will seek the child to destroy him" (Matthew 2:13).

episodes.title: The Escape to Egypt and the Boy in the Temple
episodes.description: From a perilous night flight to Egypt, through a king’s cruel decree, to a twelve‑year‑old Jesus astonishing teachers in the temple, this episode reveals the early trials and triumphs of the Holy Family.
episodes.summary: Joseph awoke from a dream in which an angel warned, "Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, for Herod will seek the child to destroy him" (Matt 2:13). By night he led Mary and the infant Jesus on a silent journey, crossing the desert and arriving safely in Egypt, where they lived under God’s protection. In Egypt, King Herod, enraged by the loss of the newborn king, ordered the slaughter of all boys two years old and under in Bethlehem (Matt 2:16). The tragic event is recounted briefly, emphasizing the cruelty of the decree. After Herod’s death, an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Rise, take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the child's life are dead" (Matt 2:19‑20). The family returned and settled in Nazareth, fulfilling the prophecy that He would be called a Nazarene. When Jesus was twelve, his parents took him to Jerusalem for the Passover feast. On the journey home, Mary and Joseph realized he was missing and searched for three days, finally finding him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers. He answered them, "Did you not know that I must be about my Father's house?" (Luke 2:49), leaving all who heard him amazed at his understanding and answers. The episode closes with a note that Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man, as the years passed.

episodes.title: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus
episodes.description: John the Baptist's urgent call awakens the world, and the Son of God steps into the Jordan to be baptized, marking the launch of His public ministry.
episodes.summary: John the Baptist, dressed in a rough camel‑hair garment, stands on the banks of the Jordan, proclaiming, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near” (Matt 3:2). He baptizes crowds, telling them, “I have baptized you with water, but he who comes after me is mightier than I… He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit” (Matt 3:11). The people listen, and many come to be baptized, hearing his promise that one far greater is about to appear. Jesus, about thirty, arrives at the Jordan and asks John to baptize Him. John protests, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” (John 1:26), but Jesus replies, “Let it be so now; for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness” (Matt 3:15). As Jesus rises from the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice declares, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (Mark 1:11). Immediately after the voice, the Spirit drives Jesus into the wilderness (Mark 1:12), where He will be led to begin His mission. The episode ends with the Holy Spirit guiding the newly anointed Messiah into the desert, setting the stage for the trials and triumphs to come.

episodes.title: Jesus Tempted in the Wilderness
episodes.description: After His baptism, Jesus faces the ultimate test in the desert, confronting Satan’s lies with Scripture and emerging victorious.
episodes.summary: Led by the Holy Spirit, Jesus is driven into the wilderness. He fasts for forty days and forty nights, feeling intense hunger. During this time He remains in prayer, trusting the Father. Satan, the shadowy tempter, approaches and first tempts Him to turn stones into bread, saying “If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become food.” Jesus answers, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God’.” Next Satan challenges Him to throw Himself from the temple, quoting Scripture, “If you are the Son of God, jump, for the angels will rescue you.” Jesus replies, “It is written, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test’.” Finally Satan offers all the kingdoms of the world if Jesus will bow and worship him; Jesus retorts, “It is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve’.” With those words Satan departs, and angels descend to minister to the weary Son. Jesus rises from the desert, his spirit renewed, and walks back toward the Jordan. There John the Baptist sees Him and declares, “Behold the Lamb of God!”

episodes.title: The First Disciples
episodes.description: Jesus gathers his first followers, calling them to a new purpose, and leads them toward the miracle of a wedding at Cana.
episodes.summary: Andrew, a former disciple of John the Baptist, follows Jesus and spends the day listening to His teaching. He brings his brother Simon to meet the Messiah, and Jesus looks at Simon and says, "You are Simon, son of John; you shall be called Cephas (Peter)." Meanwhile, Philip, moved by what he has heard, comes to Jesus and brings his friend Nathanael, who skeptically asks, "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" Jesus replies, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree I saw you," convincing Nathanael of His divine insight. That evening, on the shore of the Sea of Galilee, the disciples have spent the night without a single catch. Jesus stands by the water and says, "Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch." Peter obeys, and the nets fill so abundantly that they begin to tear. Jesus looks at the astonished fishermen and declares, "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men." Peter, Andrew, James, and John leave their boats at once, following Him. As the new disciples gather with the risen sun, Jesus turns to them and says, "Let us go to the wedding at Cana." The invitation points them toward the first sign that will reveal His glory, setting the stage for the miracle to come.

episodes.title: Jesus Turns Water into Wine
episodes.description: From turning water into wine at a humble wedding to driving out the merchants from the holy Temple, Jesus begins His public ministry with bold signs and daring action, culminating in a secret night visit from the curious Pharisee Nicodemus.
episodes.summary: The episode opens at a wedding in Cana of Galilee where the hosts run out of wine. Mother Mary approaches Jesus, saying, "Do whatever he tells you," and He instructs the servants to fill six stone jars with water. He then tells them to draw some out and bring it to the master of the banquet, and the water has become the finest wine, revealing His first sign and causing the disciples to believe in Him. During Passover in Jerusalem, Jesus enters the Temple courts and finds merchants and money changers profiting from the holy place. He overturns the tables, scattering the coins, and declares, "Do not make my Father's house a market." The crowd is stunned as the Temple is cleansed, underscoring His authority over religious practice. Later that night, Nicodemus, a respected Pharisee, comes to Jesus in secret, seeking understanding. He approaches quietly, and the episode ends with his arrival, setting the stage for a deep conversation about the Kingdom of God.

characters.name: Jesus
characters.role: the Son of God, the Messiah
characters.look: Jesus: a man of about thirty with a gentle, compassionate face, warm olive skin, shoulder-length dark brown hair and a short beard, kind dark eyes, a simple off-white linen robe with a deep red mantle over one shoulder, sandals

characters.name: Mother Mary
characters.look: Mother Mary: a young Jewish woman with a gentle, serene face and olive skin, a light blue head covering over a simple cream robe

characters.name: Nicodemus
characters.role: a Pharisee and member of the council
characters.look: Nicodemus: an older Pharisee with a grey beard in fine blue and white robes with a prayer shawl

setting: First-century Judea and Galilee under Roman rule: the village of Nazareth, Bethlehem, the shores and fishing boats of the Sea of Galilee, the Jordan river, the desert wilderness and Jerusalem with its great temple.
